record.original_question: Fix r > 0 and a compact set M \subset \mathbb{R}^d. A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for M is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. For dimensions d \ge 3, must every maximal distance minimizer \Sigma be representable as a union of finitely many injective curves?

evidence.quote:
For a given compact set M ⊂ Rd and a given positive number r > 0, consider the problem of finding a connected compact
set Σ of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H1 ) such that

                                M ⊂ Br (Σ),

where Br (Σ) denotes the closed r-neighborhood of the set Σ. We refer to such a set Σ as a Maximal distance minimizer
(MDM or r-minimizer).
Question 1.4. Is any MDM in Rd a union of a finite number of injective curves? Open for d ≥ 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\geq 3$, fix $r>0$, and let $M\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a nonempty compact set. For any set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, denote by $B_r(A)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:\operatorname{dist}(x,A)\leq r\}$ its closed $r$-neighborhood, and let $\mathcal{H}^1$ denote the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure. A connected compact set $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is called a maximal distance minimizer (or $r$-minimizer) for $M$ if $M\subset B_r(\Sigma)$ and $\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma)$ is minimal among all connected compact sets satisfying this covering condition. An injective curve means the image of a continuous injective map from a closed interval into $\mathbb{R}^d$.

Question: Must every maximal distance minimizer $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ (for any compact $M$ and any $r>0$) be representable as a union of finitely many injective curves?
artifact.status_search_result: In dimension 2, every maximal distance minimizer is known to be a finite union of simple (injective) curves. For $d\geq 3$, the analogous structural question remains open; only partial local regularity results are known (e.g., bounds on the number of tangent rays at a point and lower bounds on angles between them).

status_evidence.title: On regularity of maximal distance minimizers in Euclidean Space
status_evidence.snippet: Local regularity results for MDMs in $\mathbb{R}^d$, including bounds on tangent rays and angles, but no global finite-curve decomposition.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-dimensional regularity is only partially understood.

status_evidence.title: An overview of maximal distance minimizers problem
status_evidence.snippet: Planar MDMs are finite unions of simple curves; corresponding statement in higher dimensions is not established.
status_evidence.claim: The 2D case is solved; the $d\geq 3$ case is not.
